chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who returns from his journey after the 'Asr prayer in the month of Ramadan, and he has intercourse with his wife when she has become pure from her menses. Is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with her? He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أ يُوَاقِعُهَا: does he have sexual relations with her
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a traveler to have sexual intercourse with his wife after returning from travel during Ramadan if she is pure from menstruation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar clarifies that a traveler who breaks his fast in Ramadan may resume marital relations after 'Asr, provided he has completed his purification from menstruation. It highlights the flexibility in fiqh regarding the resumption of daily obligations for travelers, distinguishing between the act of intercourse and the state of ritual purity. The ruling underscores that the prohibition on daytime intercourse is lifted once the fast is broken, even if the full day has not yet elapsed.
